title: Step 1 - a generic stack
intro: Type the ghost text. Mistakes turn red;
fix them with any vim motion.
`Stack[T any]` is generic: `T` is a type parameter, so
one `Stack` holds ints, strings or anything else, and
`Stack[int]` only ever holds ints. The values live in a
slice; the top is its last element.
`Pop` and `Peek` return `(T, bool)`, the comma-ok form:
on an empty stack there is no value to give, so they
`Pop` sets the slot it vacates to the zero value before
shrinking the slice. The array behind the slice keeps
that slot, so a pointer left there would keep its value
alive and the garbage collector could never reclaim it.
Indentation is inserted for you on `<Enter>`.
